exposure: being in communities with pastoralist region
outcome: prelacteal feeding (giving anything other than breast milk during the first 3 days after birth)
cohort: The study included a weighted sample of 24,252 neonates in Ethiopia, drawn from the Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey 2019 data.
finding: Giving anything other than breast milk to newborns was significantly associated with individual factors such as Catholic religion and timely initiation of breastfeeding, as well as community-level factors including cesarean delivery usage and living in pastoralist regions.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery usage was found to be a significant predictor, increasing the odds of neonates receiving anything other than breast milk.
cross-section timing: within the first 3 days after birth
